traps.desc: reversed the order, writing oats to milk instead of milk to oats

problems.desc: Student must say that Kim wrote the numbers in the wrong order: the quantity named first (milk) must come first, so milk to oats is 5 to 3, not 3 to 5.
Explanation must show both ratios reduced to the same simplest form (both 4/6 and 10/15 simplify to 2/3), or an equivalent multiplier argument, so Jon is right.

traps.desc: divided hours by miles instead of miles by hours

problems.desc: Student must name the mistake: Leo divided hours by miles (3/120) instead of miles by hours, so his number is hours per mile, not miles per hour.

traps.desc: added 4 to the previous milk value (6) instead of keeping the 2:3 ratio

problems.desc: Student must circle (or name) the third column, the one pairing 6 cups of rice with 10 cups of milk, as the entry that breaks the 2:3 pattern.

traps.desc: flipped one side of the proportion, solving 2/8 = 12/x instead of 2/8 = x/12

problems.desc: Explanation must say that Mia's proportion matches cups to muffins on one side and muffins to cups on the other: both fractions must keep the same order (cups over muffins), giving 2/8 = x/12.

traps.desc: added the same 6 to both parts of 3:4 instead of multiplying, giving 9:10

problems.desc: Student must pick out 9:10 as the ratio that is not equivalent to 3:4 (6:8 and 15:20 both simplify to 3:4; 9:10 does not).

Explanation must say that Raj compared two different kinds of ratios: water per syrup for one punch against syrup per water for the other. A fair comparison uses the same order for both, e.g. syrup per water: 3/7 versus 4/9, and 3/7 is smaller, so punch B tastes stronger.

traps.desc: copied the 8 from the next column instead of scaling the 5:2 ratio
added 4 to the previous bottom entry (8) instead of scaling the ratio

problems.desc: Explanation must describe the test applied to each column: divide the top entry by the bottom one (or simplify the column ratio) and check that it equals 5/2; the columns for 15 and 25 fail the test.
